{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=physical+mechanisms+of+record+robustness+decoherence+noise+threshold&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"OSI Stack Redesign for Quantum Networks: Requirements, Technologies, Challenges, and Future Directions.\", \"abstract\": \"Quantum communication is emerging as a foundation for next-generation networks, offering unprecedented capabilities in security, entanglement-based connectivity, and distributed computation. However, the classical Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model, designed for deterministic, error-tolerant systems, is incompatible with quantum phenomena such as decoherence, probabilistic entanglement, and the no-cloning theorem. This paper surveys and redefines the OSI model for quantum networking in the context of 7G systems. We propose a Quantum-Converged OSI stack by extending the classical seven-layer model with two additional layers: (i) Layer 0, the Quantum Substrate, responsible for entanglement management, coherence preservation, and teleportation; and (ii) Layer 8, the Cognitive Intent Plane, which enables AI- and QML-driven orchestration. The survey synthesizes over 150 research works published between 2018 and 2025, classifying them by OSI layer, enabling technologies (e.g., Quantum Key Distribution, Quantum Error Correction, and Post-Quantum Cryptography), and application domains such as satellite quantum links, quantum IoT, and federated edge systems. We further provide a taxonomy of cross-layer enablers and discuss simulation tools, including NetSquid, QuNetSim, and QuISP. Finally, an evaluation framework with quantum-native metrics, such as entropy throughput, coherence latency, and entanglement fidelity, is introduced, along with open challenges for programmable stacks, digital twins, and AI-defined quantum agents. The specific and novel contribution of this work is a Quantum-Converged OSI stack that extends the classical seven-layer model with two additional layers: Layer 0, the Quantum Substrate, responsible for entanglement management, coherence preservation, and teleportation; and Layer 8, the Cognitive Intent Plane, which enables AI- and QML-driven orchestration. Decomposition-Indexed Classicality: An A/R/F Framework for Observer-Dependent Quantum Experience
Authors/Creators
Almon, Ricardo
(Producer)
Contributors
Producer:
Almon, Ricardo
Description
This work develops a quantitative framework for
observer-dependent classicality
in quantum mechanics based on three operational functionals:
Redundancy (R)
,
Accessibility (A)
, and
Observer Flow (F)
. The A/R/F framework distinguishes environmental redundancy from the effective redundancy usable by a specific observer, models accessibility through a noisy-threshold aperture function, and introduces a continuity measure governing an observer’s capacity to integrate records over time. Classicality becomes a
decomposition-indexed property
, not a global feature of the universal wavefunction.
Applied to
Wigner’s Friend
and
Frauchiger–Renner
, the framework dissolves paradoxes by showing that cross-agent inferences fail precisely in regimes where effective accessibility is low. The paper outlines experimental signatures, including observer-dependent classicality thresholds and flow-disruption tests, offering a route toward
empirical constraints on observer-relative quantum structure
.

summary: Quantum Darwinism and spectrum broadcast structure describe the emergence of objectivity in quantum systems.
